title: Partition Array into Disjoint Intervals
statement: Cut the integer array `nums` into a non-empty prefix (the left part) and the non-empty remainder (the right part) so that no value in the left part is larger than any value in the right part. Among all such cuts, choose the one with the shortest left part and return that left part's length. The inputs guarantee that at least one valid cut exists.
constraints: At least one valid cut exists
notes:
## Intuition

A cut after position `i - 1` is valid exactly when the largest value of `nums[0..i-1]` is at most the smallest value of `nums[i..]`. Checking every pair of values for every cut costs O(n²) or worse. Precomputing running minimums from the right and keeping a running maximum from the left turns each check into one comparison.

## Approach

1. Fill `suffixMin[i]` with the smallest value of `nums[i..n-1]`, scanning right to left.
2. Start `prefixMax` as `nums[0]`, the largest value of a left part of length 1.
3. For each `i` from 1, the cut puts `nums[0..i-1]` on the left. If `prefixMax <= suffixMin[i]`, the cut is valid and `i` is the shortest such length, so return it.
4. Otherwise extend the left part by `nums[i]` and update `prefixMax`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [5, 0, 3, 8, 6]` gives `suffixMin = [0, 0, 3, 6, 6]`. At `i = 1`: `prefixMax = 5 > 0`. Add `0`; `prefixMax` stays 5. At `i = 2`: `5 > 3`. Add `3`; still 5. At `i = 3`: `5 <= 6`, so the answer is `3` (left `[5, 0, 3]`, right `[8, 6]`).

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass to build `suffixMin`, one pass to find the cut.
- Space: O(n) for `suffixMin`.

## Pitfalls

- Use `<=`, not `<`: equal values may sit on both sides.
- Compare `prefixMax` with `suffixMin[i]` before adding `nums[i]` to the left part; otherwise the left part is one element too long.
- Both parts must be non-empty, so the scan starts at `i = 1` and stops before `n`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `nums` |
| `suffixMin[i]` | smallest value from index `i` to the end |
| `prefixMax` | largest value in the current left part `nums[0..i-1]` |
| `i` | length of the left part being tested (first index of the right part) |

narration.3: suffixMin[i] will hold the smallest value from index i to the end.
narration.4: The last suffix holds only the last value.
narration.5: Scan from right to left to build the suffix minimums.
narration.6: Each suffix minimum is the smaller of this value and the minimum after it.
narration.9: The left part starts as just nums[0], so its maximum is nums[0].
narration.10: Try left parts of length i, so the right part starts at index i.
narration.11: The cut is valid when the left maximum is no bigger than the right minimum.
narration.12: Lengths are tried in increasing order, so the first valid one is the shortest.
narration.14: Not valid yet: move nums[i] into the left part and update its maximum.
narration.16: Unreachable for valid input, since a cut is guaranteed.
